message.content: I've reviewed the artifact context: an RMSNorm forward kernel in Triton, straightforward single-block-per-row implementation. I'll record the initial description model covering contract, kernel model, risks, scope, and open questions.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Per-row RMSNorm forward: mean_square = sum(x*x)/n_cols, rstd = 1/sqrt(mean_square + eps), y = x * rstd, per problem.txt.", "Float32 accumulation is required for the sum of squares.", "Inputs may arrive at different storage precisions (fp32, or the same data after a bf16 round-trip); output contract is presumably fp32.", "Rows whose magnitude is close to zero are in scope, so eps behavior near mean_square ~ 0 matters.", "Reference implementation: Liger-Kernel _rms_norm_forward_kernel (single-pass forward, no weight/bias)."], "kernel_model": ["One Triton program per row (grid = num_rows); row_idx cast to int64 to avoid 32-bit offset overflow (kernel.py line 17, 34).", "Loads the row with a mask (BLOCK_SIZE = next_power_of_2(n_cols)), pads masked lanes with 0.0, and casts to float32 before reduction (line 20).", "Reduction is tl.sum(X*X)/n_cols in fp32, then rsqrt(mean_square + eps) via libdevice (lines 21-22); rstd stored to a per-row RSTD buffer (line 23).", "Python wrapper always upcasts X to fp32 (X32 = X.float(), line 31) and allocates an fp32 Y of shape (num_rows, n_cols); returns only Y, not RSTD.", "Assumes 2D contiguous or at least row-stride-passed tensors; Y is newly allocated so Y.stride(0) is n_cols.", "No explicit guard for n_cols == 0, num_rows == 0, or BLOCK_SIZE overflow for huge n_cols."], "risk_map": ["Near-zero rows: if mean_square + eps underflows or rsqrt precision differs from torch's 1/sqrt, output error could be amplified; verify against the specified formula's numerical behavior.", "bf16 round-trip inputs: wrapper's X.float() upcast preserves the bf16 values, so reduction accuracy on already-rounded data should still match an fp32-accumulated reference — but check whether the expected reference also upcasts or computes in bf16.", "Mean-square computed by summing masked 0-padded lanes is mathematically equivalent (padded zeros contribute nothing), but n_cols is used as divisor, not BLOCK_SIZE — confirm no accidental division by BLOCK_SIZE semantics.", "rsqrt from libdevice may differ in ulps from torch.rsqrt / 1/torch.sqrt; tolerance-sensitive tests could flag this.", "Non-contiguous input strides: only stride(0) is passed; assumes stride(1) == 1 for both X32 (guaranteed since X32 = X.float() produces a copy? not guaranteed if X already fp32 — X.float() returns the same tensor when dtype already fp32, so a strided fp32 input would keep its stride(1)).", "eps passed as a Python float runtime argument, not constexpr — fine numerically, but eps=0.0 with an all-zero row gives rsqrt(0) = inf; contract says rows close to zero are in scope, not exactly zero — check whether exactly-zero rows are tested."], "open_questions": ["Does the test harness compare against a torch reference computed with the same upcast order (x.float() before reduction) or on native input dtype?", "What tolerance is used, and is it relative per-element or global allclose?", "Are exactly-zero rows or eps=0 cases included in the test distribution?", "Does the harness ever pass non-contiguous or higher-dimensional inputs to rms_norm_forward?", "Is RSTD expected as part of the returned contract (Liger returns rstd for backward), or is Y alone sufficient here?"], "scope_notes": ["Single forward pass only; no backward/gradient, no weight/bias parameters in this variant.", "In-scope: precision variants (fp32, bf16 round-trip), near-zero rows, fp32 accumulation semantics.", "Out-of-scope unless test code says otherwise: ragged/batched 3D inputs, in-place output, fused ops."], "summary": "Initial description of case_04: Triton RMSNorm forward kernel matched against Liger-Kernel reference semantics."}
